title: Metabolically and epigenetically reprogrammed splenic TRNP1hiCD8+ T cells exacerbate liver fibrosis.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Zenodo record 20001905 (CC-BY-4.0): 16 figure source-data xlsx files of 9-24 KB each plus 8 western-blot PDFs; opened SourceData_Fig1.xlsx, whose sheet Fig1h is 57 rows of spleen-to-body-weight ratios by group (ND = normal diet). GEO metadata: GSE298189 (mouse scRNA-seq, single-cell RNA sequencing) has 6 samples and only a RAW.tar; GSE295165 (bulk RNA-seq) has 6 samples with one normalized-counts file (MCD diet vs normal diet).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That the human sequencing data sit in GSA-Human HRA017433 (China's controlled-access archive, which normally needs an access application), the SomaScan proteomics in OMIX016768, and that the other 13 GEO series (ATAC-seq, CUT&Tag, bisulfite sequencing, Hi-C) are similarly small mechanistic experiments. I did not open those series.

a1_downloadable.note: Mouse GEO series and Zenodo source data download openly (checked). Human data in GSA-Human HRA017433 normally needs an access application (paper text only), so the human side fails A1.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No outcome table exists. The source data are per-figure group summaries; any cell-level label (TRNP1-high CD8+ T cell state) would have to be built by clustering the scRNA-seq (single-cell RNA sequencing) data yourself.

a3_inputs_present.note: Expression counts are present (one bulk normalized-counts file, scRNA-seq raw tar), checked in GEO metadata.

a4_units_stated.note: Source data columns are named (e.g. 'Spleen to body weight ratio'), checked in Fig1h.

a5_enough_rows.note: The biggest source-data sheet opened has 57 rows; bulk RNA-seq series have 6 samples each and scRNA-seq has 6 samples. The independent unit is the mouse or the diet condition, so there are only tens.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: under 1 GB for the processed files
a6_fits_laptop.note: Small files; the raw Hi-C and bisulfite data would not be used.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: GEO series list matches the data availability statement; per-sample counts were not cross-checked against the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: Group labels (diet model vs normal diet) are experimental conditions, not model outputs.

backbone.name: scGPT or Geneformer (single-cell foundation models) would be the only fit

honest_claim_h3: With 6-sample mouse experiments, no model claim is possible beyond restating the paper's group differences.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use spleen immune cell gene expression to predict whether a mouse has diet-induced fatty liver disease with fibrosis.
plain_idea.train_on: Single-cell or bulk gene expression from mouse spleen or T cells; 6 samples per GEO series (verified in metadata), cell counts unknown.
plain_idea.predict: Diet condition (fatty-liver diet vs normal diet) or a pro-fibrotic T cell state, which would have to be defined by clustering rather than measured.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Would test whether the spleen carries a readable signature of liver fibrosis, but six animals per condition can't support that.

label_elsewhere.why: Not assessed because Part A failed.

ml_idea: None viable: this is a mechanistic mouse study with small, many-assay experiments (n=6 per series) and per-figure summary tables, not an ML-scale labelled dataset.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; rejected at Part A.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count samples per GEO series: done, 6 each, which kills it.

verdict_reason: Fails A5 and A2. It's a mechanistic mouse study: each GEO series has 6 samples, the Zenodo source data are small per-figure group summaries (the largest sheet opened has 57 rows), there's no outcome column, and the human data sit in a controlled-access archive.
